processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Alloy ingots with nominal composition Fe-35Mn-19Al-5Cu (at.%) produced from raw materials of high purity (>99.9 %).
Hot-rolled into plates with a thickness of 4 mm.
Plates cut into 10×5×2 mm3 samples for Vickers hardness measurements and microstructure characterizations.
Aging at 575 °C for 6 h followed by water quenching; one of the aging conditions applied between 525 °C and 650 °C for 1, 3, 6 and 10 h.

structures.overall_structure: After aging at 575 °C for 6 h the 19Al alloy consists of a largely β-Mn matrix; the α matrix has essentially transformed to β-Mn and the surface appears as a featureless matrix at the SEM scale.

interfaces.phase_evolution: α → α + FCC Cu-rich phase → α-Mn + β-Mn + BCC phase → β-Mn + BCC phase + FCC Cu-rich phase.
interfaces.interface_notes: For the Fe-Mn-Al-Cu low-density steels a new BCC phase and an FCC Cu-rich phase form at the interfaces between β-Mn in the ultra-hard alloys; the amount of FCC Cu-rich phase between β-Mn interfaces decreases with increasing Al content. These are general findings for the alloy family and are not resolved for the specific 19Al 575 °C/6 h condition (whose SE surface is largely featureless).

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Vickers hardness measured with a load of 9.8 N for 15 s; each sample tested 5 times and the values averaged.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: load 9.8 N for 15 s; each sample tested 5 times and averaged
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure the Vickers hardness of the aged samples, including the 19Al alloy after each aging treatment.
characterization_methods.key_findings: The 19Al alloy aged at 575 °C for 6 h exhibits a Vickers hardness of 835.4 ± 30.9 HV.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: ZEISS Sigma 300 SEM operated at 5 kV
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Main fields with 50 µm scale bars; 10 µm insets
characterization_methods.purpose: Identify the precipitation of secondary phases such as α-Mn and β-Mn in the aged samples.
characterization_methods.key_findings: For the 19Al alloy aged at 575 °C for 6 h the SE image shows a featureless, largely β-Mn matrix marked with a β-Mn label.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: GeminiSEM 300 SEM; scanning step size 1.5 µm (low magnification) and 0.05 µm (high magnification)
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine the constituent phases (α, β-Mn, α-Mn, BCC, FCC) of the solution-treated and aged alloys.
characterization_methods.key_findings: EBSD of the 19Al alloy (Fig. 6) shows the α→β-Mn transformation with aging plus new BCC and FCC Cu-rich precipitates within β-Mn; the specific 575 °C/6 h condition is not among the EBSD-mapped 19Al conditions (525 °C/10 h, 600 °C/3 h, 650 °C/6 h).

characterization_methods.purpose: Identify the phase compositions (α/D03, α-Mn, β-Mn) of the alloys after selected aging treatments.
characterization_methods.key_findings: XRD (Fig. 10) shows α/D03 together with both α-Mn and β-Mn for the selected samples; the 19Al trace was measured at 550 °C/6 h, not at the extracted 575 °C/6 h condition.

unmapped_findings: Hardness of the 19Al alloy reaches its maximum of 917.8 HV at 600 °C/10 h (not at the extracted 575 °C/6 h condition, which gives 835.4 HV); the paper's fracture-toughness (KIC = 3.5 MPa·m1/2 for 19Al), nanoindentation hardness (10.4 ± 1.3 GPa), intrinsic β-Mn hardness (12.5 ± 0.4 GPa) and TEM interface analyses (Figs. 11–12) all refer to the hardest samples (19Al = 600 °C/10 h, 15Al = 600 °C/6 h, 17Al = 575 °C/6 h), not to the 19Al 575 °C/6 h condition.

For the 19Al alloy, the amount of Al dissolved in β-Mn measured by SEM-EDS in its hardest sample is 17.5 at.% (Mn 36.2 at.%, Cu 2.6 at.%), which the paper links to solid-solution strengthening of β-Mn; this composition is reported for the hardest (600 °C/10 h) sample rather than the 575 °C/6 h condition.

Increasing Al content slowed the β-Mn precipitation kinetics in these alloys: for the 19Al alloy the α→β-Mn transformation was complete only after ~10 h at 550 °C, untransformed α was still observed after 3 h at 575 °C, and at 600 °C and above the transformation completed within 1 h.

The Fe-Mn-Al-Cu low-density steel series shows an ultra-wide adjustable hardness from 253.4 HV to 965.6 HV through simple aging; the 15Al alloy (Fe-35.2Mn-15Al-5.2Cu) achieved an ultra-high specific hardness of 141 HV·cm3/g. No specific-hardness value is reported for the 19Al 575 °C/6 h condition.
